title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a Grothendieck manuscript. It is a typed page, 'page 6-43, n° 392', from a Bourbaki rédaction (draft) on commutative algebra, covering the different, the complementary module and Gorenstein-type conditions. It sits between handwritten pages on the functional equation of L-functions, so it is most likely misfiled or reused paper. The setting comes from 'exerc. 2', not visible here. A is a Noetherian (presumably Krull or Dedekind-like) domain, B is the integral closure of A in a finite separable extension, and C is an intermediate ring (an 'order'). C* is the complementary module (inverse different) {x : Tr(xC) ⊂ A}, and D_{C/A} is the Dedekind different. 'Pseudo-invertible' means invertible after localizing at every height-one prime of A, in the sense of divisorial / Krull theory.

(e) C* is pseudo-invertible iff for every height-one prime p of A, (D_{C/A})_p : (D_{C/A})_p = C_p.

4a) Let C be a Noetherian domain, q a p-primary ideal with q:q = C. Then q:p ⊂ C, and q is irreducible iff (q:p)/q is a simple C-module. Reduce to C Artinian local with q = 0. There 0:p is the socle, and 0 is irreducible iff the socle is simple. In modern terms, the Artinian ring C/q is Gorenstein.

4b) C* is pseudo-invertible iff for every height-one p of A, the primary components of pC_p in C_p are irreducible. Reduce to A a DVR with uniformizer π. C* is invertible iff each C*/m_iC* is simple. Equivalently, using (ab)* = a*:b, each (πC:m_i)/πC is simple. Since πC:m_i = q_i:m_i, conclude by (a). Modern reading: for one-dimensional orders, the canonical (dualizing) module ω ≅ C* is invertible iff C is Gorenstein iff C/πC is Gorenstein.

4c) C*_p/C_p ≅ C_p/(D_{C/A})_p for all height-one p iff C* is pseudo-invertible. This is the Gorenstein condition expressed through the different.

4d) C_p = B_p for all height-one p iff every nonzero primary ideal of C is pseudo-invertible. The hint is to use p² for a prime p.

5) Let K be a number field with ring of integers B. Every order C in K has invertible C* (i.e. is Gorenstein) iff [K:Q] ≤ 2. The text breaks off at the hint for the quadratic case, which uses D_{C/Z): quadratic orders are monogenic, so C* = f'(α)^{-1}C. For degree ≥ 3, an order such as Z + pB is not Gorenstein.
errors: 4a hint says 'c'est un (A/p)-module'. In this exercise there is no A, so it should read (C/p)-module. This is a typo in the typescript.
The condition q:q = C is used to get q:p ⊂ C, via xq ⊂ xp ⊂ q. That argument is correct as stated.
'prop. ' in exercise 5 has a blank cross-reference, normal for a draft.

ideas.what: An Artinian local ring with 0 irreducible iff its socle is simple; irreducible primary ideal iff (q:p)/q is simple
Complementary module C* invertible iff the order is Gorenstein; criterion via primary components of pC_p and via the different
ideas.modern_name: Gorenstein orders; the canonical module equals the inverse different
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dedekind; Bass 'On the ubiquity of Gorenstein rings' (1963)

ideas.what: Every order in K is Gorenstein iff [K:Q] ≤ 2
ideas.modern_name: Ubiquity of Gorenstein orders in quadratic fields

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typed Bourbaki draft page (n° 392) of standard exercises on Gorenstein orders and the different, all known (Bass 1963), and likely misfiled among the L-function notes. Its only interest is archival: a Bourbaki rédaction among Grothendieck's papers.
transcription_corrections: The page is typewritten, not handwritten. It is a Bourbaki draft fragment 'n° 392', page 6-43, unrelated to the surrounding handwritten L-function pages.
'(A/p)-module' in 4a matches the typescript but is an original typo for (C/p)-module.
Handwritten '21' at the bottom left is the archive page number.
